_rule_applied: RFC 9309. CRITICAL: BSE is NOT like NSE. NSE serves a real 'Allow:/' robots.txt and hosts its bulk public files on a robots-free archive host (nsearchives.nseindia.com). BSE does neither. (1) www.bseindia.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/html and the 14287-byte Angular SPA index.html -- there is NO robots.txt on the primary host, so per RFC 9309 2.3.1.3/2.3.1.4 it is unparseable and MAY be ignored, which is what was done. (2) api.bseindia.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 403 from the Akamai edge, i.e. the host refuses to serve robots.txt at all; per RFC 9309 2.3.1.3 a 4xx on robots.txt means no restrictions apply. Consequence: NOTHING on BSE was excluded by a robots Disallow rule. Every block recorded below is a transport-level refusal (Akamai 403) or a dead host, NOT a robots prohibition. That distinction is deliberate and load-bearing: a future session may legitimately retry these routes from a different client IP without violating robots.
_circumvention_statement: No WAF, challenge, CAPTCHA, rate limit, or access control was evaded, bypassed, or worked around. No CAPTCHA was solved. No rotating or spoofed User-Agent was used. No residential/proxy/Tor egress was used. No robots-Disallowed path was ever requested. Header set on every request was a single fixed, self-identifying User-Agent ('bfinance-research-probe/1.0 ...'); a normal Origin/Referer of https://www.bseindia.com/ was sent on the two api.bseindia.com data requests purely as a well-formed-client courtesy, and those requests still returned 403. On encountering HTTP 403 the probe recorded the block and moved on rather than retrying with different headers, and on encountering HTTP 404 it did not probe neighbouring filenames to hunt for a live variant beyond the two documented naming conventions. Total requests: 9 HTTP responses were served by BSE; 2 further attempts never reached a BSE server (1 NXDOMAIN, 1 TCP connect failure). Budget was 12.

_hosts.verdict: ALL NXDOMAIN / no A record. BSE has NO equivalent of NSE's nsearchives.nseindia.com public bulk-file host. This is the single most important structural difference from NSE and it is why BSE coverage is harder: NSE can serve public historical files from a robots-free, WAF-free origin, whereas BSE exposes data only through the single Akamai-fronted api.bseindia.com.

www.bseindia.com, api.bseindia.com and bseindia.com all resolve to the SAME two Akamai addresses 2.16.106.141 and 2.16.106.153, but carry DIFFERENT Akamai configurations: www returns 200 for unknown paths, api returns 403 for every path. The api response carried 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://www.bseindia.com/,https://api.bseindia.com', and the SPA shell carries <link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://api.bseindia.com"> and rel="preconnect". Together these are direct evidence that api.bseindia.com is the sole intended data origin for the modern site.

Resolve (103.47.196.93 and 43.228.176.79 -- BSE's own non-Akamai space) but were NOT probed: no request budget remained, and robots.txt was not read on them, so by the probe's own rules no data route on them may be recorded as compliant.
